You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the monoclinic space group P2₁ (space-group number 4, Hall symbol P 2yb). The supplied input cell is a primitive monoclinic cell with lattice parameters a = 4.766247 Å, b = 4.763173 Å, c = 9.23102724 Å, α = 89.95201469°, β = 90.0°, and γ = 90.0°, so the input cell is very slightly non-orthogonal through α while β and γ remain exactly right angles. The declared input composition is Fe₆O₆F₆, corresponding to 18 atoms in the input cell.

All fractional coordinates below are given in the input frame. The standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, with the origin shift s = (0, 0, 0). The transformation matrix P has first row (0, −1, 0), second row (1, −6.119282658351607×10⁻¹⁷, 0), and third row (4.494761524288699×10⁻²⁰, −6.669854648281051×10⁻²⁰, 1). Thus, to within the tiny numerical off-diagonal terms, the standard-frame x coordinate is the negative of the input y coordinate, the standard-frame y coordinate is essentially the input x coordinate, and the standard-frame z coordinate is the input z coordinate, with no origin translation. The very small coefficients of order 10⁻¹⁷ to 10⁻²⁰ are numerical residues rather than physical displacements.

In P2₁, every independent atom listed here occupies a general 2a orbit with coordinate relation (x, y, z), so each representative position generates one symmetry-equivalent partner under the twofold screw operation. There are three independent iron orbits, three independent oxygen orbits, and three independent fluorine orbits, giving nine independent representative atoms and eighteen atoms total.

The first iron sublattice is represented by Fe at fractional position (0.287205, 0.462343, 0.416613). The second independent iron sublattice is represented by Fe at (0.221032, 0.526615, 0.749337). The third independent iron sublattice is represented by Fe at (0.202635, 0.506600, 0.084161). These three Fe representatives are distinct in all three fractional coordinates, so they define separate iron layers or sites rather than a single repeated iron position.

The oxygen atoms likewise form three independent 2a sublattices. One oxygen representative is O at (0.055246, 0.322912, 0.913416), a second is O at (0.068156, 0.311786, 0.253916), and the third is O at (0.429390, 0.673560, 0.582702). The first two oxygen representatives have relatively similar x and y values but very different z values, while the third oxygen orbit is shifted to much larger x and y.

Fluorine also occupies three independent 2a sublattices. The representative fluorine positions are F at (0.049877, 0.289457, 0.582999), F at (0.442842, 0.711619, 0.918643), and F at (0.456770, 0.695110, 0.248654). As with oxygen, two of these fluorine orbits cluster at larger x and y values near 0.44–0.46 and 0.70–0.71, while the remaining fluorine orbit lies at much smaller x and y.

Taken together, the input cell contains six Fe atoms from the three independent Fe 2a orbits, six O atoms from the three independent O 2a orbits, and six F atoms from the three independent F 2a orbits. The atomic arrangement is therefore fully specified by nine independent representative positions in the slightly monoclinic input cell, repeated by the P2₁ symmetry to give the complete Fe₆O₆F₆ structure. No precision corrections beyond the stated six-decimal rounding are required.
